title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: What's the best reaction you've ever had to your works of art?

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: We asked Harry how he comes up with his ideas and where he gets his inspiration from.

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: “I create 'kosmotronics' – which are works of art made from plastic waste.

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: My work ranges from little water pistols to dust busters and from hard hats to big plastic Easter eggs – every last little bit of plastic is put to good use.

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: People don't always believe that my works of art are made almost entirely from plastic.

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: Sometimes I'm commissioned to produce a work of art, in which case the final product will depend on what my client wants.

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: For example, I was once asked to turn a hard hat into a hanging work of art.

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: The client wanted the shape of the hard hat to be recognisable, but for the ultimate piece to be intended for a very different use.

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: People often give me material, or I'll find it somewhere.

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: Sometimes, I'll have it lying around in a corner somewhere for half a year before I finally get round to using it.

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: Because a lot of my pieces are quite small, my preferred equipment to use is a Dremel multi-tool with a flexible shaft.

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: I find this attachment a lot more versatile and manageable than other tools.”

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: “I discovered, by coincidence, that polishing works very well with soft plastics.

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: However, soft plastic melts faster, so it’s wise to use a slower rotation speed.

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: The polishing wheel creates a soft and smooth surface, because of which paint sticks easier too.

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: A great way to kill two birds with just one stone!”

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: I really wanted to be part of the event, but you have to pay to exhibit there.

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: Thanks to crowdfunding, I was eventually able to participate and exhibit two works of art as it would cost more to exhibit a third piece.

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: I decided to opt for a different approach, I wore one of my works of art: a kosmotronic hard hat!

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: The event was attended by a total of 450 artists, but within no time at all, everyone was talking about my hard hat.

title: Maker: Harry Arling | Dremel
text: That was quite a smart thing to do, even if I do say so myself.

text: Start with light pressure and gradually deepen the engraving until you’re satisfied with the results.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Installing laminate flooring can completely transform your space, and with the Dremel US20V, the process becomes easier and more precise.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Follow this step-by-step guide to achieve a perfect fit, with a focus on how to use your Dremel US20V for fine detailed sawing and making clean, professional cuts.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Before you start sanding, you’ll want to check your window frame for wood rot, a fungus that eats away wood.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Wood rot can compromise the structure of the frame.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: First up, remove the frame from its hinges and lay it on your workbench.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Using the sharp, pointed tool known as an awl, start tracing along the edges and crevices of the wood.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Make sure to check for soft spots, which signify wood rot.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Anywhere the awl easily pierces the surface of the wood – bingo, you’ve found rot!

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Before you can clean out the wood rot, first remove old paint from the window frame.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: You can easily do this using a triangle paint scraper.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Scrape over the whole frame with the tool until you’ve removed all the loose paint.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Don’t worry if the surface isn’t smooth – we’ll get to the sanding later on.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Using the pointed side of the scraper (or the awl), scrape out the rot you found in step 1.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: This is the first stage of rot removal – we’ll guide you through a more thorough cleaning in the next step.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Thoroughly removing rot helps to ensure the structural integrity of your frame and prevents future rot from developing.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Before you pick up your Dremel Multi-Tool, put on your safety gloves, goggles, earmuffs and dust mask.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Attach Router Bit 6,4 mm (640) to the Multi-Tool.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Start at a low RPM (rotations per minute) – such as 10.000 or 15.000 – and begin to rout the places you scraped away in step 2.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Rout away all wood rot and don’t worry about roughness: the sanding will smooth everything out.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Check out How to Avoid Failures While Sanding for more tips like these.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: After routing, it’s time to start sanding the wood.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Insert the Flap wheel 4,8 mm (504) into your Dremel Multi-Tool.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: This time, you can set the RPM a little higher than you do when routing – say around 20.000.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Keep your safety gear on, and start sanding the surface of the wood.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Focus on sanding the holes created by the removal of the wood rot.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Keep sanding until the edges of the routed holes are smooth and ready to be filled.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: The goal now is to patch up all the holes and restore the frame’s uniform surface.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Two-component epoxy filler is great for this because it hardens well and it’s water-resistant.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Start with the base filler on your pallet knife and add a squeeze or two of the second component.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Using another pallet knife, mix them together until the filler is consistent in both color and texture.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Press it into any holes or gaps, filling one at a time.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Wipe away any excess filler with the side of the pallet knife and let the filler dry.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Don’t worry about getting it perfectly smooth – you’ll be sanding soon.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: The next step is to prepare the frame for painting by sanding it.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Wearing your safety equipment, start with an orbital sanding tool.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: This way, you can sand all the top surfaces at once.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Then switch to your Dremel Multi-Tool and attach the Sanding Band 120 grit (432) .

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Starting with a low RPM and light pressure, begin in the hard-to-reach places, such as corners and edges.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Pay attention to the areas with filler, ensuring a smooth transition between filler and wood.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: You don’t need to remove all of the old paint – the goal is a smooth, splinter-free surface that’s ready for paint.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Now that you’ve used a sanding tool to smooth the frame, it will be quite dusty.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Grab your dust mask and use a bristle brush to remove most of the surface dust.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: You could also use a vacuum cleaner for this part.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Next up, fill a small bowl with a mix of water and degreaser – the degreaser packaging should have instructions for the correct ratio.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Dip a dry cloth into the mixture and rub down the window frame first, before cleaning the glass.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Finally, ensure your work surface is dust-free so your paint job is perfect.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: No matter how confident you are in your painting ability, taping up the glass ensures a neat finish.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Top tip: use a strong, good quality tape so it doesn’t leave adhesive behind when you remove it later.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Is your frame made up of lots of small windows, like ours?

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Simply tape over the wood using one long piece of tape.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Then use a packing knife to neatly slice away the tape that’s covering the cross-sections of wood you’ll need to paint.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: See the video at the top of this page to learn exactly how.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: You’ve reached the very last step in the restoration of your window frame.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Give the paint a good stir and then start by painting all the tricky edges with a small brush.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: A brush is also handy for the frame’s sides.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Next, use a roller brush for the flat topsides.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: For the best result, paint two thin layers, letting one layer dry before the next.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: When the final layer has dried, remove the tape.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Before doing so, score the edges with the packing knife to cut through any dried paint and ensure clean removal.

title: Step-by-Step: Restore an Old Window Frame | Dremel
text: Finally, attach your frame to the window and admire your handiwork!
